Description: Every eligible decision on the CURRENT engine emits what was chosen, what else was permitted, the probability assigned, and what the fallback would have done. This is the one capability that cannot be backfilled.
As the platform, I need a single schema for every decision the engine makes, so that decisions from different decision points are comparable and joinable.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Schema covers: decision point id, strategy id and version, chosen action, permitted action set, propensity assigned to the chosen action, fallback action that would have fired, population context, timestamp, transaction and customer identifiers.
• Schema is versioned and additive-only.
• Reviewed and signed off by Architecture and Analytics Engineering.

Summary: Emit decision records from the routing engine (D6)
Description: As an analyst, I need every routing decision logged with its counterfactual, so that routing strategies can later be evaluated off-policy.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Every D6 decision on eligible traffic emits a record.
• No change to the routing decision itself — output is byte-identical to today for a control sample of 1M transactions.
• Record includes the permitted processor set and the fallback processor.

Summary: Emit decision records from the retry engine (D4.2)
Description: As an analyst, I need retry decisions logged with what else was permitted, so that retry strategies become evaluable.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Every D4.2 decision emits a record, including no-action decisions.
• Retry behaviour unchanged.
• Retry records link to the parent authorization attempt.

Summary: Emit decision records from credential selection (D4.1)
Description: As an analyst, I need credential selection logged with the alternative credential, so that Experiment 1 has a counterfactual to report.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Every D4.1 decision emits a record naming the credential presented and the credential not presented.
• Credential values are tokenised in the record — no PAN in the event store.
• Credential selection behaviour unchanged.

Summary: Assign and document propensity for deterministic strategies
Description: As an analyst, I need a stated propensity convention for deterministic strategies, so that off-policy estimators are not silently mis-specified later.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Deterministic strategies record propensity 1.0 on the chosen action and 0 on the alternatives.
• Convention is documented alongside the schema, with the implications for off-policy evaluation stated.
• A strategy class field distinguishes DETERMINISTIC from future stochastic classes.

Summary: Record the fallback action without executing it
Description: As the platform, I need to know what the fallback would have done, so that attribution is possible without running two flows.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Fallback resolution runs in shadow and never dispatches.
• Added latency measured and within the agreed budget.
• Fallback field is never null for a decision that has a registered fallback.

Description: As an analyst, I need at least four quarters of history, so that seasonality can be separated from effect.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Records land in the event store within 60 seconds of the decision.
• 13-month retention configured and cost-modelled.
• Partitioned for efficient replay by date range and decision point.

Summary: Block synthesised propensity in downstream jobs
Description: As a reviewer, I need the platform to refuse reconstructed propensity, so that an evaluated result is never quietly based on a guess.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Any job writing a propensity value for a record that did not carry one is rejected.
• Rejection is logged and alerts the strategy owner.
• Documented as a platform invariant, not a lint rule.

Summary: Verify record completeness against transaction volume
Description: As a reviewer, I need proof that the evidence layer is not silently dropping decisions, so that a later readout is trustworthy.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Daily reconciliation: decision records vs eligible transactions, by decision point.
• Completeness at or above 99.5%.
• Shortfall below threshold raises an alert with the missing population identified.

Summary: SPIKE: measure added latency of decision-record emission
Description: As the platform owner, I need to know what the evidence layer costs in latency before it goes to full traffic, so that the authorization path is not degraded.
Acceptance Criteria:
• p50, p95 and p99 added latency measured at production-representative volume.
• Result compared against the agreed latency budget.
• Recommendation on synchronous vs asynchronous emission, with the trade-off on completeness stated.

Description: A 2% population reserved before the first experiment runs, excluded from experiments and from exploration, with a creation date that cannot be edited.

Summary: Define holdout eligibility and the assignment rule
Description: As the platform owner, I need a stated rule for who is in the holdout, so that it is defensible and stable over time.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Eligibility defined at customer level, with the population and exclusions written down.
• Assignment is a deterministic hash — same customer, same answer, forever.
• Rule reviewed by Analytics Engineering for representativeness against the total population.

Description: As the platform, I need holdout membership computed the same way everywhere, so that it cannot drift between services.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Assignment implemented once and consumed by every caller.
• Same customer resolves identically across regions.
• Membership resolvable in under 1ms.
Blocked By: Define holdout eligibility and the assignment rule

Summary: Exclude the holdout from experiments and from exploration
Description: As a reviewer, I need the holdout untouched by any learning activity, so that it measures the platform rather than the experiments.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Holdout members are never enrolled in any experiment.
• Holdout members are never selected for exploration traffic.
• An attempt to include them fails closed and raises an alert.

Summary: Persist holdout membership with an immutable creation date
Description: As a reviewer, I need to prove when the holdout was reserved, so that the claim that it pre-dates the experiments is verifiable.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Creation date recorded at first assignment and not editable by any role.
• Membership history retained for the life of the platform.
• Audit log for any membership change.

Description: As an analyst, I need to see holdout composition and drift, so that a divergence from the general population is caught early.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Weekly report: volume, merchant mix, geography mix, card mix vs the non-holdout population.
• Alerts on material composition drift.
• Report retained as evidence alongside readouts.
Blocked By: Persist holdout membership with an immutable creation date

Summary: Document the holdout as a governed, non-resizable asset
Description: As the platform owner, I need a stated rule that the holdout cannot be quietly resized, so that its value is not eroded under delivery pressure.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Written policy: resizing or reconstituting the holdout requires a named approval from the platform owner.
• Policy referenced in the experiment registration gates.

Description: Agree what the decision points are, what each may choose from, and what a route can actually support. Scope and schema only — the build is D60.

Summary: Catalogue the current decision points and permitted action sets
Description: As an architect, I need a written inventory of where the payment flow makes choices, so that the registry describes reality rather than an ideal.
Acceptance Criteria:
• All five current decision points documented: D4 gate, D4.1 credential, D4.2 retry, D5 authentication, D6 routing.
• Permitted action set enumerated for each, as implemented today.
• Gaps between documented and actual behaviour listed explicitly.

Description: As an architect, I need a model of what each route and processor can actually support, so that a strategy cannot select an option that will fail downstream.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Capability dimensions defined: credential forms accepted, authentication methods, currencies, MCCs, network tokens, retry semantics.
• Model distinguishes contractual capability from technical capability.
• Reviewed with Network and Processor Management.

Summary: Agree the registry schema and versioning approach
Description: As an architect, I need the registry to be bitemporal, so that we can answer both what is true now and what was true when a decision was made.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Schema covers valid time and knowledge time.
• Versioning and deprecation rules written down.
• Signed off by Architecture.
Blocked By: Catalogue the current decision points and permitted action sets

Summary: SPIKE: survey processor capability data availability
Description: As an architect, I need to know which capability facts we can obtain and which we will have to assert, so that the D60 verification work is correctly sized.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Each processor surveyed for available capability data and format.
• Gaps listed with an estimate of effort to close.
• Recommendation on which facts must be verified vs may be asserted with an expiry.

Summary: Publish the registry scope decision for sign-off
Description: As the programme, I need the registry scope agreed before it is built, so that D60 is a build rather than a design.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Scope document published naming what is in and out of the first registry.
• Architecture sign-off recorded.
• Out-of-scope items carried to the D90+ backlog rather than dropped.
Blocked By: Agree the registry schema and versioning approach

Description: The five ownership boundaries named, the exploration budget bounded, the economic objective expressed in a usable form, and the consent posture settled.

Summary: Assign and document the five ownership boundaries
Description: As the programme, I need named owners for the five decisions that bound the platform, so that they are not re-litigated every quarter.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Named owner recorded for: economic objective, exploration budget, decision-point registry, exposure authority, exploration consent.
• Each owner has confirmed in writing.
• Escalation path defined where two owners disagree.

Summary: Define the exploration budget in basis points, with a ceiling
Description: As Product, I need a stated budget for what learning costs, so that exploration is a decision rather than an accident.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Budget expressed in bps of qualifying volume, per quarter.
• Hard ceiling defined, above which an experiment cannot start.
• Consumption tracked and reported against the budget.
Blocked By: Assign and document the five ownership boundaries

Summary: Define the economic objective form by pricing model
Description: As Product and Finance, I need the approval-versus-cost trade-off expressed in a form a strategy can actually consume, so that BALANCED is a real posture rather than a label.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Objective expressed as an exchange rate: bps of cost accepted per 100 bps of approval.
• A value agreed separately for interchange-plus and for blended pricing.
• Documented with worked examples in both directions.
Blocked By: Assign and document the five ownership boundaries

Summary: Legal review of exploration consent posture
Description: As the programme, I need to know whether a knowingly weaker arm on a named client needs contractual consent, so that Experiment 1 does not stop at the last gate.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Legal opinion recorded on running a deliberately degraded arm on live merchant traffic.
• Position stated for existing contracts and for new ones.
• If consent is required, the consent artefact and the signing path are defined.
Blocked By: Assign and document the five ownership boundaries

Summary: Define the experiment review forum and decision rights
Description: As the programme, I need a standing forum with stated decision rights, so that promotion and abort decisions are made rather than escalated.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Forum membership, cadence and quorum defined.
• Decision rights stated: who may promote, who may abort, who may widen exposure.
• First meeting scheduled.
Blocked By: Assign and document the five ownership boundaries

Description: A strategy becomes a registered, versioned artefact with an owner, a fallback and an expiry — deployable without an engineering release.
As a strategy owner, I need a strategy to be a declared artefact rather than code, so that it can be reviewed, versioned and retired without a release.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Schema: id, version, decision point, class, population predicate, definition, fallback strategy reference, owner, expiry.
• Fallback is mandatory and must reference a registered strategy.
• Owner and expiry are mandatory.
Blocked By: Agree the registry schema and versioning approach

Description: As a strategy owner, I need to register a strategy without an engineering release, so that the change cycle is days rather than quarters.
Acceptance Criteria:
• API accepts a strategy artefact and returns a registered version.
• CLI wraps the API for the common path.
• Registration is rejected with a specific, actionable message when a field is invalid.

Description: As a reviewer, I need a registered version to be unchangeable, so that a readout always refers to a known artefact.
Acceptance Criteria:
• A registered version cannot be edited — a change produces a new version.
• Prior versions remain resolvable indefinitely.
• Attempted edit is rejected and audited.

Description: As the platform owner, I need strategies to expire, so that nothing lingers unowned in the decision path.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Expiry is mandatory at registration, with a maximum of 180 days.
• Warnings to the owner at 30 and 7 days.
• An expired strategy stops being bindable; flows already bound to it fall back and alert.

Description: As a strategy owner, I need a clean way to retire a strategy, so that losing variants do not accumulate.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Retirement blocks new bindings and reports which flows still reference the strategy.
• Retirement is reversible within 30 days, then permanent.
• Retired strategies remain resolvable for historical traces.

Description: As a reviewer, I need strategy names to describe what they do, so that a trace is readable a year later.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Registration rejects opaque names such as Strategy1 or Test_A.
• Convention documented with positive and negative examples.
• Existing names migrated before D60 exit.

Description: A flow binds exactly one strategy at every decision point, and the compiler refuses to build a variant that differs from its baseline at more than one.
As a strategy owner, I need a flow to name exactly one strategy at every decision point, so that there is no implicit behaviour in the path.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Schema: flow id, version, baseline reference, one binding per decision point.
• An unbound decision point is a compile error, never a default.
• Baseline reference is mandatory for a variant flow.

Description: As the platform, I need flows compiled and validated before they exist in production, so that a broken flow cannot be exposed.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Compiler resolves every binding to a registered, unexpired strategy version.
• Compilation fails on any unbound or unresolvable decision point.
• Compiled output is deterministic — same input, same artefact.

Description: As a reviewer, I need the compiler to refuse a variant that differs from its baseline at more than one decision point, so that attribution is guaranteed rather than assumed.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Compiler computes the diff against the named baseline.
• A diff count other than 1 for a variant flow is rejected with the differing points named.
• Rejection cannot be overridden by a flag.

Description: As the platform, I need flows cryptographically signed, so that what runs in production is what was reviewed.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Every compiled flow is signed at build.
• Runtime verifies the signature before resolution and refuses an unsigned or altered flow.
• Key rotation procedure documented.

Description: As the platform, I need a new flow available in every region quickly, so that promotion is not a deployment.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Bundle distributes to all regions with p99 under 60 seconds.
• Distribution is observable, with per-region confirmation.
• A region that fails to receive a bundle alerts and continues on last-known-good.

Summary: Regional flow resolution with last-known-good fallback
Description: As the platform, I need every region to resolve flows locally, so that a control-plane outage cannot stop authorization.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Flow resolution is local, with no synchronous control-plane call on the authorization path.
• Last-known-good bundle serves if the control plane is unreachable.
• Staleness is measured and alerted beyond an agreed threshold.

Description: A candidate flow runs against logged decision records and produces an exact count of decisions that would change, and for whom, before any live exposure.
As a strategy owner, I need to run a candidate flow against traffic that already happened, so that I know its blast radius before exposing anyone.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Harness replays a compiled flow against a date range of decision records.
• Nothing is dispatched — no processor, network or merchant call is made.
• Replay is reproducible: same flow, same window, same result.

Summary: Exact changed-decision count and affected population report
Description: As a reviewer, I need to know precisely how many decisions change and for whom, so that promotion is a measured step rather than a leap.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Report gives an exact count of decisions that would differ, not an estimate.
• Affected population broken down by merchant, geography and card type.
• Count expressed as a percentage of eligible traffic.

Description: As a compliance reviewer, I need to know whether a candidate flow would violate an existing policy, so that regulatory constraints are not discovered in production.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Replay evaluates the candidate against the active policy set.
• Any conflict is reported with the policy, the authority and the affected population.
• A conflict blocks promotion.

Summary: Replay report as a promotion gate artefact
Description: As the platform, I need the replay report attached to the promotion record, so that the evidence travels with the decision.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Promotion requires a replay report against a window of at least 30 days.
• Report is immutably attached to the promotion record.
• A stale report, older than 14 days, is rejected.
Blocked By: Exact changed-decision count and affected population report

Description: As a reviewer, I need the limits of replay stated plainly, so that nobody treats a backtest as a result.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Written statement: replay tells us which decisions would change, never whether they would have been approved.
• Statement appears in the replay report itself, not only in a wiki.
• Replay output is never merged with experiment output in any report.

Description: Registration pre-declares hypothesis, metric, effect size, direction, population, weights and stopping rule — and the gates that catch a broken design are mechanical, not a reviewer.
As an experiment owner, I need to pre-declare the design, so that the result cannot be re-framed once it arrives.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Schema: hypothesis, single primary metric, effect size, direction, population predicate, arms and weights, randomisation unit, assignment point, stopping rule, guardrails.
• Direction is mandatory.
• Primary metric is singular — a list is rejected.

Description: As an experiment owner, I need the duration derived from the effect size and the weights, so that experiments end on evidence rather than on a calendar.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Calculator takes baseline rate, effect size, weights, power and alpha, and returns required enrolments per arm.
• Unequal allocation handled correctly — a 95/5 split is not treated as 50/50.
• Output is stored on the experiment artefact and drives the stop condition.

Summary: Gate: treatment must be deliverable to the whole test arm
Description: As a reviewer, I need qualification checked against what the treatment needs, so that part of the test arm cannot silently fail to receive it.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Gate verifies that every member of the qualifying population can receive the variant treatment.
• Qualification on the control credential alone is rejected when the treatment requires another.
• Rejection names the unreachable sub-population.

Description: As a reviewer, I need the experiment gates to reuse the compiler check, so that there is one definition of a valid comparison.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Registration rejects an experiment whose arms differ at more than one decision point.
• Gate calls the compiler diff rather than reimplementing it.

Summary: Gate: randomisation unit appropriate to the treatment
Description: As a reviewer, I need per-transaction randomisation blocked for credential-form changes, so that we do not create the risk signal we are trying to measure.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Gate rejects per-transaction randomisation where the treatment changes credential form or authentication behaviour.
• Rejection explains the issuer-behaviour reason.
• Customer-level and merchant-level units supported.

Description: As a reviewer, I need the design frozen once traffic moves, so that the hypothesis cannot follow the data.
Acceptance Criteria:
• No field on the experiment artefact is editable after the first enrolment, except exposure weights within the pre-declared ramp.
• An attempted edit is rejected and audited.
• Amendments require a new experiment with a stated relationship to the original.

Description: As the platform, I need one active experiment per layer and segment, so that two experiments cannot silently contaminate each other.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Ledger records every active experiment against a controlled segment vocabulary.
• Registering a second experiment on an occupied (layer, segment) is rejected with the conflicting experiment named.
• Ledger is queryable and reported weekly.

Description: The decision-point and capability registries built and verified with processors rather than asserted, and enforced as a capability filter at decision time.
As the platform, I need the decision points registered rather than implied by code, so that a strategy can be bound to one without an engineering change.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Registry built to the agreed schema, bitemporal.
• All five current decision points registered.
• Adding a decision point is a registry change, not a code change.
Blocked By: Publish the registry scope decision for sign-off

Description: As the platform, I need to know what each route can actually support, so that a strategy cannot choose an option that will fail.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Registry built to the agreed capability model.
• Capabilities carry a source and an expiry.
• An expired capability fact degrades to unsupported rather than to assumed-supported.

Description: As an architect, I need capabilities verified rather than asserted, so that the capability filter is trustworthy.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Each processor capability confirmed with the processor or by controlled test.
• Unverifiable facts marked as asserted, with an expiry and an owner.
• Verification status visible in the registry and in any trace that used it.

Summary: Enforce the capability filter at decision time
Description: As the platform, I need unsupported options removed before a strategy chooses, so that a strategy never has to know about downstream limits.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Capability filter runs ahead of strategy evaluation at every decision point.
• Filtered-out options appear in the decision record as not-permitted, with the reason.
• Filter adds under 1ms at p99.

Description: Promotion is decoupled from exposure, assignment is deterministic at the divergence point, and traffic moves by changing a number rather than by a deployment.
As a strategy owner, I need a flow to reach production at zero percent, so that promotion is safe and reversible by construction.
Acceptance Criteria:
• A promoted flow is resolvable in every region and receives no traffic until an exposure record says so.
• A flow can sit at 0% indefinitely without expiring.
• Promotion changes no merchant behaviour and requires no deployment window.
Blocked By: Regional flow resolution with last-known-good fallback

Summary: Deterministic assignment at the divergence point
Description: As an analyst, I need assignment to happen at the last node common to all arms, so that transactions that could never receive the treatment are not diluting the measurement.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Assignment occurs immediately before the first differing decision point, not at context assembly.
• Assignment is deterministic on the randomisation unit — same unit, same arm, for the life of the experiment.
• Transactions that never reach the divergence point are not enrolled.

Description: As an analyst, I need every attempt in a transaction to stay in the same arm, so that a retry cannot cross arms and corrupt the result.
Acceptance Criteria:
• All attempts within a transaction resolve to the assigned arm.
• Assignment is recorded on the first attempt and reused, never recomputed.
• A cross-arm retry is impossible by construction, and any occurrence alerts.
Blocked By: Deterministic assignment at the divergence point

Description: As an experiment owner, I need to change exposure by changing a number, so that ramping and stopping do not require a release.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Weights changeable at runtime, taking effect within one propagation cycle.
• Change is audited with actor, time and prior value.
• Weights cannot be moved outside the pre-declared ramp without a documented override.

Description: As an analyst, I need transactions that fell back to stay in their assigned arm but be flagged, so that intent-to-treat and per-protocol can both be reported.
Acceptance Criteria:
• A transaction that could not receive its assigned treatment remains in its arm and is flagged.
• Fidelity rate computed per arm and reported live.
• A fidelity floor is enforced as a promotion gate.

Summary: Exposure authority controls and audit trail
Description: As the platform owner, I need exposure changes restricted to named roles, so that traffic does not move without accountability.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Only holders of the exposure authority role may change weights.
• Every change is audited and visible in the experiment record.
• Emergency abort is available to on-call without the full role.

Description: Exposure, pace and guardrails visible in real time, with an arm removed from allocation automatically within one propagation cycle on breach.
As an experiment owner, I need to see enrolment pace against the target, so that a stalled or runaway experiment is visible immediately.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Dashboard shows qualifying volume, per-arm enrolment, actual vs target share, and projected days to sample size.
• Refresh under five minutes.
• Available to the review forum without a request.
Blocked By: Deterministic assignment at the divergence point

Description: As an experiment owner, I need guardrails computed continuously, so that harm is detected in hours rather than at readout.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Computes approval gap, fraud proxy, dispute proxy, cost of acceptance, per-merchant harm and latency, per arm.
• Each guardrail has a declared threshold on the experiment artefact.
• Computation lag under 30 minutes.

Description: As the platform owner, I need a breaching arm removed from allocation without a human in the path, so that the blast radius is bounded by the system rather than by a meeting.
Acceptance Criteria:
• A guardrail breach removes the arm from allocation within one propagation cycle.
• Abort requires no approval and cannot be blocked.
• Aborted arms cannot be re-enabled without a documented review.

Summary: Abort floor on the effect itself
Description: As the platform owner, I need an experiment to stop if the effect is far worse than expected, so that a deliberately weaker arm cannot run away.
Acceptance Criteria:
• An effect-size floor is declared on the experiment artefact alongside the guardrails.
• Breaching the floor aborts the arm on the same path as a guardrail breach.
• Floor is mandatory for any experiment whose declared direction is negative.

Description: As Client Service, I need to know if the cost of an experiment is concentrating on one merchant, so that a portfolio-level pass does not hide an individual loss.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Guardrails evaluated per merchant as well as in aggregate.
• A merchant breaching individually is removed from the experiment without aborting it entirely.
• Client Service is notified with the merchant and the measured impact.

Description: As the review forum, I need to know immediately when an arm aborts and why, so that the next decision is informed.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Abort notifies the experiment owner, the platform owner and Client Service within five minutes.
• Post-abort report states the breached guardrail, the measured value, the affected population and the exposure at abort.
• Report attached to the experiment record.

Description: Any transaction explained end to end — experiment membership, arm, flow, every decision applied and what the baseline would have decided — self-serve, in under two minutes.
As support and product, I need to retrieve every decision applied to a transaction, so that explaining an outcome does not require an engineer.
Acceptance Criteria:
• API returns, for a transaction: experiment membership, arm, flow and version, every decision point with the strategy applied, the action chosen and the fallback that would have fired.
• Response under two seconds at p95.
• Available for any transaction within the retention window.

Description: As support, I need to answer "why did this transaction do that" myself, so that explanations are not an escalation.
Acceptance Criteria:
• A non-engineer can go from transaction id to full explanation in under two minutes.
• Tested with five users from Client Service, unassisted.
• Links to the strategy and flow artefacts that were in force.

Summary: Trace shows experiment membership and propensity
Description: As an analyst, I need membership and propensity visible per transaction, so that an individual case can be reconciled against the aggregate.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Trace shows in-experiment yes/no, experiment name, arm, assignment unit, assignment point, propensity and treatment-delivered flag.
• Fields match the decision record exactly — no re-derivation.

Summary: Trace shows the counterfactual per decision point
Description: As an analyst, I need the "would have" column in the trace, so that attribution is inspectable at the individual level.
Acceptance Criteria:
• For each decision point, trace shows the action chosen and the action the baseline flow would have chosen.
• The trace states plainly that this is what would have been decided, not what would have been approved.

Summary: Access control and PCI scope review for trace data
Description: As compliance, I need trace access governed, so that a debugging tool does not become a data exposure.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Role-based access defined and implemented.
• PCI scope assessment completed and signed off.
• Credential values shown as tokens or last-four only; access to full values is separately controlled and audited.

Description: Outcomes joined at four horizons, revised as later horizons land, and translated into merchant and PSP economics by pricing model.
As an analyst, I need decisions joined to outcomes as they land, so that a readout is not limited to what is known at authorization.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Joins at authorization, settlement, 30-day fraud and 120-day dispute.
• Each readout states which horizons are complete and which are pending.
• Join is idempotent and reproducible.
Blocked By: Verify record completeness against transaction volume

Summary: Readout revision as later horizons land
Description: As a decision maker, I need readouts revised rather than replaced, so that a conclusion drawn at 30 days is visibly superseded at 120.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Each readout is versioned with the horizons it covers.
• A later revision links to the one it supersedes and states what changed.
• Prior revisions remain retrievable.

Description: As a decision maker, I need approval reported alongside cost, fraud, dispute and fidelity, so that no readout can present approval alone.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Scorecard computes transaction approval, first-attempt approval, cost of acceptance, fraud proxy, dispute proxy and treatment fidelity.
• A scorecard with a missing dimension is not publishable.
• Each line shows control, variant, delta and status.

Description: As a decision maker, I need an interval rather than a point estimate, so that a result is reported with its uncertainty.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Confidence interval computed for every primary and guardrail metric.
• Stopping rule evaluated against the pre-declared sample size, never against the observed effect.
• Peeking is prevented or explicitly corrected, and which was done is stated.

Description: As Product and Finance, I need the result in money, so that the decision is commercial rather than statistical.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Translates the measured effect into merchant margin and PSP net revenue, separately for interchange-plus and blended pricing.
• Assumptions (margin rate, take rate) are named inputs, not constants in code.
• Output shows the exchange rate: bps of cost per 100 bps of approval.

Summary: Publish the readout with a date and an expiry
Description: As the platform owner, I need every published number to carry an expiry, so that a measurement does not quietly become a claim.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Readout is published with the measurement window, the baseline version and an expiry date.
• An expired readout is flagged wherever it is cited.
• Re-run cadence recorded on the readout.

Description: A winner promotes to a named population, the baseline recompiles with it bound in, and rollback is an exposure pointer change.
As a strategy owner, I need to promote a winner to a named population rather than globally, so that a result that holds for one segment is not applied to all.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Promotion targets a declared population, using the same predicate vocabulary as the experiment.
• Promotion outside the tested population requires a documented justification.
• Promotion record links to the readout that justified it.
Blocked By: Publish the readout with a date and an expiry

Summary: Baseline recompile with the winner bound in
Description: As the platform, I need the baseline to move when a variant wins, so that the next experiment measures against the current best.
Acceptance Criteria:
• A new baseline flow version is compiled with the winning strategy bound at the relevant decision point.
• The prior baseline remains resolvable for historical traces.
• Active experiments against the old baseline are flagged for re-baselining.

Summary: Rollback as an exposure pointer change
Description: As on-call, I need to reverse a promotion without a deployment, so that reversal is measured in minutes.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Rollback changes an exposure pointer only — no deploy, no data migration.
• Takes effect within one propagation cycle.
• Rehearsed in a game day before D90 exit.
Blocked By: Baseline recompile with the winner bound in

Description: As the platform owner, I need every readout retained against its baseline version, so that cumulative value can be reconstructed later.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Every readout stored with the baseline version it measured against, the population and the date.
• Record is append-only.
• Queryable to answer: what has this platform been worth since inception.
Blocked By: Baseline recompile with the winner bound in

Description: Run the first controlled experiment end to end: vault network token as control, merchant-supplied credential as the deliberately weaker variant, to an economic readout.
As the credential product owner, I need the variant strategy registered, so that Experiment 1 has a treatment.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Strategy registered against D4.1 with population, definition, fallback Cred_VaultNetworkToken_v4, owner and 180-day expiry.
• Passes all registration gates.
• Reviewed by credential product and risk.

Description: As the experiment owner, I need a variant flow that differs from the baseline at exactly one point, so that the result is attributable.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Flow compiles with diff_count = 1 against F2_VaultNWT_v6.
• Every other binding identical to the baseline.
• Flow signed and distributed to all regions at 0% exposure.

Summary: Backtest and publish the blast-radius report
Description: As the review forum, I need the exact number of decisions that would change before any exposure, so that promotion is an informed step.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Replay against at least 30 days of decision records.
• Report gives exact changed-decision count, percentage of eligible traffic and affected merchants.
• No policy conflicts introduced.
Blocked By: Replay report as a promotion gate artefact

Summary: Register the experiment and clear all mechanical gates
Description: As the experiment owner, I need the design to pass the gates rather than a reviewer, so that the review meeting discusses the hypothesis instead of the statistics.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Experiment registered with hypothesis, direction, single metric, 25 bps effect size, guardrails and abort floor.
• All mechanical gates pass without override.
• Sample size computed and duration expressed in enrolments.

Description: As Client Service, I need the participating merchant informed and consented where required, so that the experiment does not create a relationship problem.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Consent posture applied per the Legal opinion.
• Participating merchant(s) identified and briefed, with the expected exploration cost stated in bps.
• Named Client Service contact assigned for the duration.
Blocked By: Legal review of exploration consent posture

Description: As the experiment owner, I need a soak period at low exposure, so that guardrails are proven before the arm widens.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Exposure at 3% for a minimum soak of seven days.
• All guardrails computing and within threshold.
• Treatment fidelity above the declared floor.

Summary: Widen to 5% and run to sample size
Description: As the experiment owner, I need the experiment to run to its pre-declared sample size, so that the result is powered.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Exposure widened to 5% within the pre-declared ramp.
• Runs to 66,900 variant enrolments or an abort.
• No design changes after first enrolment.

Description: As leadership, I need the first end-to-end readout, so that the platform has demonstrated the outcome it was built for.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Scorecard published with all six dimensions, intervals and status.
• Economic translation for both pricing models.
• Readout carries a date, a baseline version and an expiry.
• Presented to the review forum with a promote, hold or retire decision recorded.
Blocked By: Publish the readout with a date and an expiry

Description: Provisioning decoupled from presentation so a treatment seasons before exposure — without this, Experiment 2 measures a freshly minted token rather than the vault.
As the vault product owner, I need provisioning and presentation to be separate acts, so that a token can exist without being used.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Provisioning a network token does not change which credential is presented.
• Presentation is controlled solely by the D4.1 strategy binding.
• Provisioning state visible in the decision record.
Blocked By: Emit decision records from credential selection (D4.1)

Summary: Provision ahead for the full eligible population
Description: As the experiment owner, I need tokens provisioned for control and variant alike before exposure, so that provisioning is not confounded with treatment.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Eligible population provisioned regardless of arm.
• Provisioning completes before experiment start, with a verification report.
• Provisioning cost accounted separately from exploration cost.

Summary: Define and measure a seasoning window
Description: As an analyst, I need a stated seasoning period before exposure, so that we measure the vault rather than a new token.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Seasoning window defined with evidence, not assumed.
• Experiment start gated on the window having elapsed for the eligible population.
• Window recorded on the experiment artefact.
Blocked By: Provision ahead for the full eligible population

Summary: SPIKE: quantify new-token vs seasoned-token performance
Description: As an analyst, I need to know whether token age materially affects approval, so that the seasoning window is set on evidence.
Acceptance Criteria:
• Approval rate analysed by token age on existing production data.
• Result determines the seasoning window, or shows that none is needed.
• Finding documented and attached to the Experiment 2 design.
